description: Find your 2026 Medicare IRMAA surcharge by income. Enter your 2024 MAGI and filing status to see your Part B premium (base $202.90), Part D IRMAA surcharge, and the extra you pay per year versus a standard beneficiary.
answerSnippet: In 2026 the standard Medicare Part B premium is $202.90/month. IRMAA surcharges start when your 2024 MAGI tops $109,000 (single) or $218,000 (joint), raising Part B to as much as $689.90 plus a Part D surcharge up to $91.00.
intro:
**IRMAA** — the **Income-Related Monthly Adjustment Amount** — is a surcharge that higher-income Medicare beneficiaries pay **on top of** the standard Part B and Part D premiums. For **2026**, the standard Part B premium is **$202.90 per month**, and IRMAA can push it up to **$689.90**, plus a Part D surcharge of up to **$91.00**.

The surcharge is based on your **modified adjusted gross income (MAGI) from two years earlier** — so your **2026** premium is set by your **2024** tax return (AGI plus tax-exempt interest). Crossing a bracket by even **$1** bumps you into the next tier for the whole year, which makes IRMAA a classic 'cliff.'

Enter your **2024 MAGI** and **filing status** to see your 2026 Part B premium, your Part D IRMAA surcharge, and how much **extra per year** you pay compared with a standard beneficiary.
keyTakeaway: 2026 Part B base is **$202.90/month**. IRMAA kicks in above **$109,000** (single) / **$218,000** (joint) of 2024 MAGI, across **five tiers**. At the top tier (over $500,000 single / $750,000 joint) Part B is **$689.90** plus a **$91.00** Part D surcharge — roughly **$5,844/year extra per person**. IRMAA is a per-person cliff based on income two years back.

explanation:
## How IRMAA works in 2026

```
Base Part B premium (2026) = $202.90/month
IRMAA tier                 = based on your 2024 MAGI and filing status
Part B total               = base + Part B IRMAA surcharge
Part D                     = your plan premium + Part D IRMAA surcharge
```

Your **2026** IRMAA uses your **2024** MAGI = **AGI + tax-exempt interest**. The Social Security Administration mails an IRMAA determination in late 2025 based on that return.

## 2026 IRMAA brackets (single filer)

| 2024 MAGI (single) | Part B/month | Part D IRMAA/month |
|---|---|---|
| $109,000 or less | $202.90 | $0.00 |
| $109,001 – $137,000 | $284.10 | $14.50 |
| $137,001 – $171,000 | $405.80 | $37.50 |
| $171,001 – $205,000 | $527.50 | $60.40 |
| $205,001 – $500,000 | $649.20 | $83.30 |
| Over $500,000 | $689.90 | $91.00 |

For **married filing jointly**, the income thresholds are **double** ($218,000 up to $750,000) with the same premium amounts. **Married filing separately** has its own steep schedule: over $109,000 jumps to $649.20 Part B, and over $391,000 to $689.90.

## The IRMAA 'cliff'

IRMAA is **not** phased in gradually. Go **$1** over a threshold and you pay the higher tier's full surcharge for the entire year. That is why retirees watch the edges of each bracket when timing **Roth conversions, capital gains, and IRA withdrawals**.

## Two-person households

Each spouse on Medicare pays IRMAA **individually**. A couple both in Tier 5 pays the surcharge **twice**, so the household cost is roughly double the per-person figures above.

## Appealing IRMAA

If a **life-changing event** (retirement, divorce, death of a spouse, loss of income) dropped your income after 2024, you can ask SSA to use more recent income with **Form SSA-44**.

## Disclaimer

Educational estimate using published 2026 Part B and Part D IRMAA amounts. Your Part D total also includes your plan's own premium, which varies. Confirm your determination with SSA/Medicare and consider Form SSA-44 if your income has dropped.

faq.q: What is the standard Medicare Part B premium for 2026?
faq.a: The standard 2026 Part B premium is **$202.90 per month**. Beneficiaries with higher income pay that base **plus an IRMAA surcharge** on Part B and Part D.
IRMAA starts when your **2024 MAGI** exceeds **$109,000** (single/HOH) or **$218,000** (married filing jointly). MAGI is your AGI plus any tax-exempt interest.

faq.q: Why does my 2024 income set my 2026 premium?
faq.a: IRMAA uses a **two-year lookback**. SSA sets your 2026 premium from the most recent tax return on file, which is normally your **2024** return filed in 2025.

faq.q: How much is the highest IRMAA surcharge in 2026?
faq.a: At the top tier (over **$500,000** single / **$750,000** joint), Part B is **$689.90/month** and the Part D IRMAA surcharge is **$91.00/month** — about **$5,844 more per year** than a standard beneficiary pays.

faq.q: Do married couples each pay IRMAA?
faq.a: Yes. IRMAA is assessed **per person**. If both spouses are on Medicare and in the same tier, the household pays the surcharge **twice**.

faq.q: Is IRMAA a cliff or a gradual phase-in?
faq.a: It is a **cliff**. Exceeding a bracket by even **$1** moves you to the next tier's full surcharge for the entire year — which is why income timing near a threshold matters.

faq.q: Can I appeal or lower my IRMAA?
faq.a: Yes. If a **life-changing event** (retirement, marriage, divorce, death of a spouse, work stoppage) reduced your income after 2024, file **Form SSA-44** to ask SSA to use your more recent, lower income.

faq.q: Does IRMAA include my Part D plan premium?
faq.a: No. The **Part D IRMAA** shown is only the income surcharge. You still pay your Part D **plan's own premium**, which varies by the drug plan you choose.
